summary: Implemented phase 7 of the 11-phase gate-framework refactor, closed cleanly and committed. Added gate-level concurrency to verify-deploy.sh: a new --jobs N|auto flag (default auto, nproc capped at 4; --jobs 1 is the byte-identical sequential opt-out) and gate_registry_exec_concurrent_batch, a worker-slot-pool scheduler in lib/gate-registry-lib.sh ported in shape from run-all.sh's own proven pool, with wave-barrier dependency honouring, serialized-class isolation (gate 8 runs alone), longest-first cost-class scheduling, and a VERIFY_DEPLOY_NESTED nested-invocation guard mirroring RUN_ALL_NESTED. Two real concurrency bugs were caught and fixed via this phase's own new test coverage: a naive sequential state-dump-sourcing reconciliation that silently drops every concurrently-forked gate's contribution except the last (fixed with a snapshot-once-per-group/apply-delta-per-id design), and an intermittent (~1-in-10) worker-cap violation from a mapfile/process-substitution pipeline's own unwaited background reader occasionally being reaped by the dispatch loop's first wait -n (fixed with a draining wait before the dispatch loop). Output and the final PASS/FAIL line are proven byte-identical across worker counts on both synthetic test registries and the real 23-gate registry. A full, unscoped verify-deploy.sh --findings run (auto jobs, load ~4-6/24 cores) completed in 790s with a finding set matching Phase 6's documented baseline exactly, modulo expected pre-redeploy drift for this phase's own touched files (deferred to Phase 11 per existing convention). Measured real speedup: a 7-gate moderate-cost selection went from ~70s (jobs=1) to ~43s (jobs=4). Paused at this clean phase boundary; Phase 8 (shellcheck parallelization) depends only on Phase 3 and can start cleanly from here.
